title: Al cabo de: el tiempo transcurrido

sections.content: Al cabo de (after, at the end of a period of) measures elapsed time before something happens -- useful for historical narration that needs to say not just what happened, but how long it took or how long a situation lasted. It's followed by a time expression. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Al cabo de casi dos años de guerra, unidades del ejército mataron a cientos de civiles en la aldea de El Mozote.
items.english: After nearly two years of war, army units killed hundreds of civilians in the village of El Mozote.

items.spanish: Al cabo de doce años de guerra, el conflicto había dejado unas setenta y cinco mil personas muertas.
items.english: After twelve years of war, the conflict had left some seventy-five thousand people dead.

items.spanish: Al cabo de unos meses de negociaciones, ambas partes lograron finalmente acercar sus posiciones.
items.english: After a few months of negotiations, both sides finally managed to bring their positions closer together.

items.spanish: Al cabo de una década, muchos de los responsables directos del conflicto seguían sin ser procesados judicialmente.
items.english: After a decade, many of those directly responsible for the conflict still hadn't been legally prosecuted.

sections.content: Al cabo de emphasizes the duration itself, unlike después de, which just marks sequence -- reach for al cabo de specifically when the length of time is part of the point you're making.
